subject.summary: Approximate reconstruction of the palace chapel of Louis IX (consecrated 1248): lower and upper chapels, fifteen great windows between buttresses, the flamboyant west rose, two-storey porch, stair turrets, steep lead roof with the 1853 fleche and the apse angel. Plan and elevation traced from reference images; tracery is schematic.

parts.label: Upper chapel: glass walls between buttresses

identity.feature: Upper chapel's tall stained-glass walls between deep buttresses (15 windows: 4 bays a side + 7 in the apse)
West flamboyant rose, 9 m, above the porch and below the gable
Steep lead roof with cresting, and the openwork fleche: lantern, gables with angels, crocketed spire to 75.75 m
Lower chapel: low storey with its own windows under the great glass
Two octagonal stair turrets flanking the west front, crowned by crowns of thorns and spires
Two-storey porch: four piers, wide central arches, terrace balustrade, the upper portal behind
Archangel Michael on his pedestal at the east end of the ridge
